subject: biology
title: Advantages and disadvantages of sexual and asexual reproduction
key_idea: **Sexual reproduction** gives variation, so some offspring survive a change or a disease, but it is slower. **Asexual reproduction** is fast and keeps useful features, but the identical offspring can all be killed by the same disease or change.

blocks.text: Sexual reproduction mixes genes from two parents. This section covers what that gives an organism, and what it costs.

items: It produces **genetic variation** in the offspring.
So some offspring are better adapted and survive a disease, an environmental change or a selection pressure.
Variation allows **evolution** by natural selection.
Plants make seeds that can be dispersed to new areas. The offspring can colonise new places or escape an adverse event where the parent grew.
Many seeds or offspring are made, so it is more likely that some survive.
A mate has to be found.
Fertilisation or pollination takes time, so the process is slower.
Offspring can have features that are less advantageous than those of the parents.
Variation is the key advantage: some offspring survive when conditions change.
Variation allows evolution.
It is slower and needs a mate.

blocks.text: Asexual reproduction copies one parent by mitosis. This section covers why that is quick, and why it is risky.

items: Only one parent is needed, so there is no need to find a mate or to rely on pollinators.
It is **faster**: there is no need to wait for flowers, fruits or seeds.
Many offspring are produced, and they can colonise the local area.
It uses less energy and fewer materials, because no gametes, flowers or seeds are made.
The offspring are identical, so they keep the **desired characteristics** of the parent.
The offspring are well adapted to the environment the parent already lives in.
There is no genetic variation, so there are no new characteristics.
All the offspring are susceptible to the same **disease**, so one pathogen can kill them all.
They cannot survive an environmental change if the parent could not.
The gene pool is reduced.
Asexual reproduction is fast, needs one parent and keeps useful features.
Identical offspring are all equally at risk from one disease or one change.
In an answer, say the consequence of being identical, not just that they are identical.

blocks.text: Some organisms use both types of reproduction, at different times. Each type is used when it helps most.

items: Malarial protists reproduce asexually and sexually during their life cycle.
Many fungi reproduce both asexually and sexually.
Strawberry plants reproduce sexually using flowers, fruits and seeds.
Strawberry plants also reproduce asexually using **runners**. Mitosis makes the new cells, and the parent passes sugar and water to the new plant.
Bluebells reproduce sexually by making seeds and asexually by making new bulbs.
Duckweed usually divides into two, and only occasionally reproduces sexually by growing flowers.

items: Malarial protists, many fungi and strawberry plants all use both types.
Asexual reproduction copies a successful parent. Sexual reproduction gives variation.

checks.q: Give one advantage and one disadvantage of sexual reproduction.
checks.a: Advantage: it produces genetic variation, so some offspring are more likely to survive a disease or environmental change. Disadvantage: a mate must be found, or it takes longer.

checks.q: Banana plants are grown by asexual reproduction. Explain why one disease could kill all the plants on a farm.
checks.a: The plants are all genetically identical (clones), so they all have the same genes and are all susceptible to the same disease.

checks.q: Give two advantages of asexual reproduction for a strawberry plant.
checks.a: Any two from: it is faster; many offspring are produced; only one parent is needed (no pollinators); the offspring are identical and well adapted to the environment; the offspring receive water and sugars from the parent; less energy is needed.

worked_example.question:
Bluebell plants grow in woodlands in the UK. Bluebells can reproduce sexually by producing seeds.

Explain why sexual reproduction is an advantage for bluebells.
answer_points: There is genetic variation in the offspring.
So the better adapted bluebells survive (natural selection, survival of the fittest).
Seeds are dispersed, so bluebells colonise new areas or escape an adverse event in the original area.
Many offspring are made, so there is a higher probability that some will survive.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each point. Write about bluebells: a general answer scores a maximum of 3.

worked_example.question: Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of sexual reproduction and asexual reproduction.
answer_points: Sexual reproduction, advantages: it creates variation in a species, some organisms can survive a selection pressure, and it allows evolution.
Sexual reproduction, disadvantages: a mate must be found, fertilisation or pollination takes time so the process is slower, and offspring can have features less advantageous than the parents.
Asexual reproduction, advantages: there is no need to find a mate, there is a rapid reproductive cycle, and organisms with the beneficial characteristics of the parent can be produced.
Asexual reproduction, disadvantages: there is no variation, and a selection pressure could affect all the organisms of a species.
worked_example.tip: Marked in levels. For Level 3 (5 to 6 marks) cover both types, give advantages and disadvantages, and include the consequences of being genetically identical or genetically different.

worked_example.question:
In many countries, people rely on bananas for food.
Black sigatoka is a disease of banana plants.
The disease is caused by a fungus.

Banana plants grown by farmers are usually produced asexually.
This process uses mitosis.
This means that, if one banana plant dies of black sigatoka, all the bananas can die.

Explain why.
answer_points: All the plants are genetically identical (clones), so they all have the same genes.
worked_example.tip: The mark is for the idea that the plants are all genetically identical.
